records.quote: Prove that the mixture of Gompertz and gamma distribution complies with the ordering with the highest likelihood (the likelihood ratio ordering). Assume that X and Y are two independent Random variables with probability distribution function f(x; η, β) and f(x; ψ, δ). If η < ψ and β < δ, then Λ = f(x;η,β)/f(x;ψ,δ) = [η/(1+β) e^{βx} e^{(η/β)(e^{βx}−1)} + (η²β/2) x² e^{−ηx}] / [ψ/(1+δ) e^{δx} e^{(ψ/δ)(e^{δx}−1)} + (ψ²δ/2) x² e^{−ψx}]. ... Differentiating with respect to x, ∂log[Λ]/∂x = ... Hence, [∂log[Λ]/∂x] < 0, if η < ψ, β < δ.
records.family: mixture of Gompertz and gamma (MGGD): f(x;η,β) = η/(1+β)·e^{βx}e^{(η/β)(e^{βx}−1)} + (η²β/2)x²e^{−ηx}, x>0, η,β>0
records.compared: MGGD(η,β) vs MGGD(ψ,δ) with both parameters smaller on the left

hypotheses.text: If η < ψ and β < δ

conclusion.direction: X <=lr Y, i.e., MGGD(η,β) <=lr MGGD(ψ,δ) (density ratio decreasing in x)

records.ambiguity: Unnumbered 'prove that' statement rather than a labelled theorem; typeset formulas garbled in places (exponents/signs inconsistent across printings); the conclusion claimed is the decreasing density ratio, i.e., lr order.

note: Section 10's sole ordering result is the unnumbered lr claim for the MGGD; included.
